clue.text: Flocks of birds seen around Land's End

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
the birds sit around the other piece, wrapping it on both sides

blocks.note: crows are black birds
the final letter of Land

explanation.surface: Seabirds gather in flocks at the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost point of mainland England, which makes the surface read as a place name rather than an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words work as verbs meaning to gather together in large numbers, or as nouns for big groups.

clue.text: Marx hoarding silver in the city

indicators.note: to hoard is to keep something stored inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Chico was one of the Marx Brothers
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Karl Marx stockpiles silver while living in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx suggests Karl the economist, but it is the comedian Chico Marx.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major American city on Lake Michigan in Illinois.

clue.text: Oils first used on some paintings by Bridget Riley, for example

definitions.text: paintings by Bridget Riley, for example

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word beside it

blocks.note: the opening letter of Oils
some, as in a portion, is part

explanation.surface: An observation that Bridget Riley began some of her canvases in oils.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, used on means placed on top of the next piece. Bridget Riley is a British painter famous for dazzling black-and-white patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is the style of abstract optical-illusion painting for which Riley is best known, so her works exemplify it.

clue.text: In effect, an old author's unfinished work is penetrating

indicators.note: something unfinished is missing its ending, so the last letter goes
penetrating means going into the middle of something else

blocks.note: Daniel Defoe, eighteenth-century author of Robinson Crusoe
to act is to work or operate

explanation.surface: A literary critic says an old writer's incomplete manuscript is effectively insightful.
explanation.walkthrough: Defoe loses his final E to give DEFO, then ACT goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: De facto is Latin for existing in fact or practice, whether or not officially recognised, which is what in effect means.

clue.text: Independent leader in sabre-rattling state

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so just the opening letter is wanted
rattling shakes things up so their order is disturbed
in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: the first letter of Independent
taken as written before being shuffled

explanation.surface: A political leader of independent views stands amid a nation threatening war.
explanation.walkthrough: Sabre-rattling reads as a single compound meaning threatening war, but it splits into the fodder and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a sovereign country in the Balkans, so it is a state in the political sense.

clue.text: Peers squeal when reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a different shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords protest loudly when their chamber is reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: Peers suggests the House of Lords, but here it means people of the same standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer in the general sense is someone of the same rank or ability as another, which is an equal.

clue.text: One of Hefner's playmates - Jane Doe?

blocks.note: first meaning: a hostess in a Playboy Club, dressed in rabbit ears and tail
second meaning, taken literally: a doe is a female rabbit, so a girl among bunnies

explanation.walkthrough: Jane Doe normally names an anonymous woman; the question mark invites reading Jane as a girl's name and doe as a female rabbit. Hugh Hefner founded Playboy.
explanation.definitionFit: Playboy Club waitresses wore rabbit costumes and were called by this name, and a female young rabbit fits the literal reading.

clue.text: A word spoken in a German accent, so it's alleged

indicators.note: the words are to be pronounced as a German speaker might, with W sounding as V and a rolled R

blocks.note: a word said with a German V for W and a strongly rolled R

explanation.surface: Someone reports a remark made in a thick German accent, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is a stage-German pronunciation: 'a word' becomes 'a vurrd', which is how the answer is said.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state or assert something as fact, so a thing averred has been claimed or alleged.

clue.text: Pie town, memorably

indicators.note: printer's pie is type that has been spilled and jumbled, so it signals mixed-up letters

blocks.note: taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: A place remembered for its pies.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, while Pie also works as the anagram signal for the rest. Melton Mowbray is a Leicestershire market town famous for its pork pies.
explanation.definitionFit: This English town gives its name to the classic raised pork pie, so it is memorably the pie town.

clue.text: I'm in the French capital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller announces arrival in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The French capital points to Paris, but the French is LA and capital stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru's seat of government sits on the Pacific coast, making this South American city a national capital.

clue.text: Father Ted, entertaining affected queen, may be patronised

indicators.note: affected means altered or disturbed, so the letters are moved about
a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, as for a priest
taken as written
taken as written before being shuffled

explanation.surface: Father Ted, the sitcom priest, plays host to a camp drag queen and finds himself talked down to.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is an Irish TV comedy about a priest; here Father and Ted are separate pieces placed around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or pub that is patronised is regularly visited by customers, which is to be frequented.

clue.text: Gum or nuts one started chewing

indicators.note: the way a word is started is its opening letter, so that alone is kept

blocks.note: mast is the fallen nuts of beech, oak and similar trees
the Roman numeral for one
the opening letter of chewing

explanation.surface: Someone is offered chewing gum or nuts and has begun eating one.
explanation.walkthrough: Mast is an old word for the nuts that fall from forest trees, once used to feed pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is an aromatic resin from a Mediterranean tree, chewed since ancient times, so it is a gum.

clue.text: Cart overturned on slope where knights once jousted

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, which in an across answer means read from the end

blocks.note: a tilt is a slope or slant
a dray is a low cart for heavy loads, such as beer barrels

explanation.surface: A cart has tipped over on a hillside near an old tournament ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so the cart follows the slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiltyard was the enclosed ground used for medieval tilting, the sport of charging at each other with lances.

clue.text: Worthless recital commencing with Nicolai and Offenbach overtures

indicators.note: an overture is the opening of a work, so each name gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Nicolai
the first letter of Offenbach
a recital of events is an account of them

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a concert that opens with overtures by the composers Nicolai and Offenbach.
explanation.walkthrough: Recital and overtures point to music, but recital means a narration and overtures means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-account person or thing is of no importance or value, a mainly American colloquial adjective.

clue.text: Gem of a motor bought initially by relative

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a motor is a car
the first letter of bought
an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative bought a car that turned out to be a real gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle is a red gemstone, typically a garnet cut with a rounded top rather than facets.

clue.text: Attempt to cover front of neck with tie

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
to cover something is to wrap it, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: a bid is an attempt
the first letter of neck

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide their throat with a necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind is to fasten with a cord or rope, the same as to tie.

clue.text: Fish - without water, without oxygen

indicators.note: without can mean outside, so the first piece sits outside the second

blocks.note: something without water is dry
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A fish out of water, unable to breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dory is a flat-bodied sea fish, as in John Dory.

clue.text: Central feature of unbuttoned garment

blocks.note: first meaning: the middle of the word unbuttoned is a repeated pair of letters, TT, and such a pair is called this
second meaning: a close-fitting jacket worn by men in the Renaissance

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a description of a loose jacket, but the first half is about the spelling of the word unbuttoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pair of identical items and the tight padded jacket worn in Tudor times.

clue.text: Child attending comprehensive gets good mark for addition

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
all-in means comprehensive, covering everything
G is a grade mark meaning good

explanation.surface: A pupil at a comprehensive school earns a good grade for an adding-up exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: Comprehensive suggests a British state secondary school, but here it is the adjective meaning all-inclusive.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalling is the act of adding up figures to reach a sum, which is addition in arithmetic.

clue.text: Dead men chopped and changed

indicators.note: chopped up means cut into bits and mixed about

blocks.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of bodies hacked up and altered.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to alter or revise it, so amended means changed.

clue.text: Sprog's claws

definitions.note: Read as the plural sprogs, the apostrophe being surface dressing; setters often allow this to make the clue read smoothly.

blocks.note: first meaning: sprogs are small children
second meaning: the pincers of a crab or lobster

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe makes it look like a child's claws; the two words are separate meanings. Sprog and nipper are both British slang for a young child.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both small children in informal British speech and the pincers of a crustacean.

clue.text: Native Americans from Ohio refuse to go on to Washington

blocks.note: O is an abbreviation for Ohio
to jib is to refuse to go on, as a horse does
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

explanation.surface: Native Americans from Ohio decline to travel on to Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ojibwa, also called Chippewa, are an Indigenous people of the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Propose to a patient man in a fix

blocks.note: to put up a candidate or idea is to propose it
Job is the biblical figure famed for his patience

explanation.surface: Proposing marriage to a long-suffering man while in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Fix here means a rigged outcome, not a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-up job is something secretly arranged in advance to deceive, which is a fix or rigged affair.

clue.text: Grant immunity to parliamentarian taking refuge in city abandoned by monarch

indicators.note: abandoned by means left without, so those letters are dropped
someone taking refuge in a place goes inside it

blocks.note: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon
ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP fleeing to a city the monarch has deserted is granted immunity.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword monarch; Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from an obligation or liability, which is granting immunity.

clue.text: Fictional gantry used in novel merchandising

indicators.note: used in means contained within the following words, run across their join

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A crane from a book appears in a promotional tie-in.
explanation.walkthrough: Gantry suggests a crane frame, but it is the surname of a fictional preacher, so the answer is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmer Gantry is the title character of Sinclair Lewis's novel about a hypocritical evangelist.

clue.text: Teach grizzly relative to take note

blocks.note: the black bear is a relative of the grizzly
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Instruct a grumpy family member to write something down.
explanation.walkthrough: Teach looks like a verb, but it is Edward Teach, the real name of a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Teach was the notorious early eighteenth-century pirate known by this nickname.

clue.text: Fit to run across

blocks.note: first meaning: suitable or proper, an old-fashioned adjective
second meaning: to encounter by chance

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like advice to jog over somewhere; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an archaic adjective the word means suitable, and as a verb it means to come upon someone.

clue.text: "The Outlaw" - a Greek or Egyptian citizen

blocks.note: taken as written
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A film poster title, followed by a note on the hero's nationality.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest a film title; the words are simply two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: There were ancient cities named Thebes in both Greece and Egypt, and a native of either one was so called.

clue.text: A pole that's round with poles on decks

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a rod is a pole
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A round pole and other poles stand on a ship's decks.
explanation.walkthrough: Decks suggests a ship, but it is the verb meaning decorates.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room or tree is to decorate it, and adorns means the same.
